lessons.title: Fonts, alignment, borders and fills
learn: Wrap text and Centre Across Selection instead of Merge
lessons.mac:
Format Cells: ⌘ + 1, or Format > Cells in the menu bar
Bold / Italic / Underline: ⌘ + B / I / U
Format Painter: the paintbrush on the Home tab

steps.say: This is the quarterly sales report for Sahyadri Agro Foods. It has a centred title, a dark heading row, clean borders and a double line under the totals. Nothing fancy, but it looks like something you can send to your manager.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S02-01 Done

steps.say: You'll format fonts, fills and borders, wrap long headings, centre a title without merging cells, and copy a look with Format Painter. The practice sheet is S02-01.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Bold, font size, fill and font colour
• Wrap Text, and Center Across Selection instead of Merge
• Borders, and Format Painter

Practice sheet: S02-01

steps.say: Most of this lives on the Home tab. For anything the ribbon doesn't show, press Command 1 to open Format Cells, which has tabs for numbers, alignment, font, border and fill.

acts.t:
Where the tools are
Home tab: Bold (⌘ + B), font size, Fill Color, Font Color, Wrap Text, Center, Borders, Format Painter
Format Cells (⌘ + 1): Number • Alignment • Font • Border • Fill
Alignment > Horizontal > Center Across Selection: centres without merging

steps.say: Start with the title in A1. Press Command B for bold, then click Increase Font Size three times on the Home tab, from 11 up to 16.
Most people centre a title by selecting A1 to E1 and clicking Merge and Center. It looks fine.

But now try to select only column C. Excel grabs A to E, because the merged cell spans them. Merged cells also get in the way of sorting, filtering and pasting, which is why many finance teams avoid them.

Undo with Command Z. Select A1 to E1 again and press Command 1 to open Format Cells. On the Alignment tab, set Horizontal to Center Across Selection, and click OK. Same look, but every cell stays separate.
Do the same for the subtitle in row 2: select A2 to E2, Command 1, Center Across Selection.
Now the heading row. Select A4 to E4 and press Command B. Open the Fill Color menu and pick Dark Blue from the standard colours. Then open Font Color and pick White.
E4 has a long heading. Select it and click Wrap Text, so the words wrap inside the cell instead of spilling over. Then select B4 to E4 and click Center.
Select the whole table, A4 to E11. Open the Borders menu and choose All Borders.
For the total row, select A11 to E11, press Command B, and choose Top and Double Bottom Border. Accountants read a double line as the final total.
The targets table below needs the same heading look. Select A4 to C4, click Format Painter on the Home tab, then select A14 to C14. Only the look is copied, not the text.
Double-click Format Painter instead of single-clicking, and it stays on, so you can paint several places in a row. Press Escape to switch it off.

acts.t:
Pro tip
Double-click Format Painter to keep it switched on.
Paint as many ranges as you like, then press Escape.

steps.say: On a Mac, Command 1 opens Format Cells, and Command B, I and U give bold, italic and underline. Format Painter is the paintbrush on the Home tab, and Format, Cells in the menu bar opens the same dialog.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Format Cells: ⌘ + 1, or Format > Cells in the menu bar
Bold / Italic / Underline: ⌘ + B / I / U
Format Painter: the paintbrush on the Home tab

steps.say: To recap. Use Center Across Selection, not Merge, for titles. Use Wrap Text for long headings and a double bottom border for totals. And Format Painter copies a look in two clicks.

acts.t:
Recap
• Center Across Selection, not Merge & Center
• Wrap Text for long headings; double bottom border for totals
• Format Painter copies the look, not the content

steps.say: Your challenge. Finish the targets table. Give A14 to C20 All Borders, make A13 bold, and centre it across A13 to C13. Compare with S02-01 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
• All Borders on A14:C20
• A13 bold, centred across A13:C13 (no merging)

Answer: sheet S02-01 Done

lessons.title: Number formats for rupees, percentages and dates
lessons.mac:
Format Cells: ⌘ + 1
Currency: ⌃ + ⇧ + $     Percentage: ⌃ + ⇧ + %     Date: ⌃ + ⇧ + #
Quick formats: the Number Format box on the Home tab

steps.say: Here's a GST invoice register. Dates read as day, month and year, the GST rate shows as a percentage, and the rupee amounts line up neatly. These are the same numbers as before. We only changed how they're displayed.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S02-02 Done

steps.say: You'll show dates as DD-MM-YYYY and DD-MMM-YY, turn rates into percentages, and see the difference between the Currency and Accounting formats. The practice sheet is S02-02.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Dates as DD-MM-YYYY and DD-MMM-YY
• Percentages, and the 18 vs 18% trap
• Currency vs Accounting

Practice sheet: S02-02

steps.say: A number format changes only the display. The value underneath stays the same, and that's what formulas use. You'll find every format in Format Cells, on the Number tab.

acts.t:
Format Cells (⌘ + 1) > Number
General • Number • Currency • Accounting • Date • Percentage • Text • Custom
Custom date codes: d = day, m = month, y = year
dd-mm-yyyy → 02-04-2026     dd-mmm-yy → 02-Apr-26

steps.say: On the practice sheet, the invoice dates show as numbers like 46114. That's how Excel stores a date: a count of days since 1 January 1900. It just needs a date format.
Press Command 1 to open Format Cells. Choose Custom, and in the Type box enter d d, dash, m m, dash, y y y y. Click OK. The first invoice now reads 02-04-2026.
For the due dates, a shorter style. Select C2 to C11, press Command 1, choose Custom, and type d d, dash, m m m, dash, y y. Three m's give the month's short name, so it reads 02-May-26.
Now the GST rates. Select F2 to F11, open Format Cells, choose Percentage with zero decimal places, and click OK.

Look at F7. It says 1800 percent, and the GST in that row is huge. Someone typed 18 instead of 18 percent. The percentage format shows the stored value times a hundred, and 18 times a hundred is 1800.
Type 18 with a percent sign and press Return. Excel stores 0.18, shows 18 percent, and the GST amount drops to the right figure.
Next, the taxable values. Select E2 to E11, open Format Cells, choose Currency, pick the rupee symbol for English, India, keep two decimal places, and click OK.
For the GST amount and invoice total, G2 to H11, choose Accounting instead, with the same rupee symbol.

Compare the two. Currency puts the rupee sign right next to the number. Accounting lines up every rupee sign on the left and every decimal point on the right, and shows zero as a dash, like the exempt invoice in row 6. Accounting is the usual choice for financial statements.
Look at the commas too. Depending on your region setting, Excel may group digits the international way, in thousands and millions. The next lesson builds a format that always shows lakh and crore.

acts.t:
Heads-up
Built-in formats group digits by your region setting: 2,84,500 or 284,500.
Lesson S02-03 builds a custom format that always shows lakh and crore.

steps.say: On a Mac, Control, Shift and the dollar sign applies a currency format, and Control, Shift and percent applies a percentage. The Number Format box on the Home tab has the common formats too.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Format Cells: ⌘ + 1
Currency: ⌃ + ⇧ + $     Percentage: ⌃ + ⇧ + %     Date: ⌃ + ⇧ + #
Quick formats: the Number Format box on the Home tab

steps.say: To recap. Formats change the look, not the value. Use custom codes like d d dash m m dash y y y y for Indian dates. Type percentages with the percent sign, and choose Accounting for statements.

acts.t:
Recap
• A format changes the display, never the value
• dd-mm-yyyy and dd-mmm-yy for Indian dates
• Type 18%, not 18  •  Accounting aligns ₹ signs and shows zero as a dash

steps.say: Your challenge. Show the GST rates in F2 to F11 with one decimal place, so 18 percent reads 18.0 percent. Compare with S02-02 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Format F2:F11 as a percentage with one decimal place (18.0%).

Answer: sheet S02-02 Done

lessons.title: Custom number formats, including lakh and crore
learn: Show zero as a dash, colour negatives, add units
lessons.mac:
Format Cells: ⌘ + 1 > Number > Custom
Typing ₹: Indian English keyboard, or ⌃ + ⌘ + Space (Emoji & Symbols)

steps.say: This branch revenue sheet speaks Indian. Revenue shows lakh and crore commas, marketing spend shows in thousands with a K, revenue also shows in crores, falling growth turns red, and units carry a label. Every cell still holds a real number.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S02-03 Done

steps.say: You'll write custom number formats for Indian digit grouping, K and crore labels, red negatives with a dash for zero, and units. The practice sheet is S02-03.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• ₹ 12,34,567 grouping, K and Cr labels
• Zero as a dash, negatives in red
• Units as a label, not as text

Practice sheet: S02-03

steps.say: A custom format can have up to four sections, separated by semicolons: positive, negative, zero, and text. Zero means a digit that always shows. Hash means a digit if needed. Text goes in quotes, and a colour or a condition goes in square brackets.

acts.t:
Custom format building blocks
positive ; negative ; zero ; text
0 = digit always shown     # = digit if needed
, after the digits = divide by 1,000
"Cr" = a text label     [Red] = colour     [>=100000] = condition

steps.say: Start with revenue. Select B2 to B12, press Command 1, and choose Custom.
In the Type box, enter this format. It has three parts. Numbers of one crore or more use the crore pattern. Numbers of one lakh or more use the lakh pattern. Everything smaller uses normal thousands.
Click OK. Pune now reads eighteen crore, forty-five lakh, sixty-two thousand three hundred rupees, with the commas exactly where an Indian reader expects them.

Marketing spend is easier to scan in thousands. Select C2 to C12 and use this format. The comma after the digits divides by a thousand, and the K in quotes is a label. Eight lakh forty-five thousand shows as 845.0K.
A comma can only divide by a thousand, and a crore is ten million, so column D already divides revenue by one crore with a formula. Give it the format rupee, 0.00, space Cr. Pune shows 18.46 Cr.
For growth, use three sections: positive, negative and zero. Negatives turn red, and zero shows as a dash. Mumbai, Aurangabad and Ratnagiri now stand out in red, and Nagpur's zero is a quiet dash.
Now the units. Nagpur's figure was typed as 1250 units, with the word. It sits on the left, so it's text, and the total in F12 quietly leaves it out.
Type just 1250 and press Return. The total in F12 goes up by one thousand two hundred and fifty.
Now add the word with a format instead. Select F2 to F12 and enter hash, comma, hash hash zero, then space units in quotes. The label shows, and the numbers still add up.
Your custom formats are saved in the workbook, at the bottom of the Custom list. To reuse one on another sheet, copy it with Format Painter.

acts.t:
Pro tip
Custom formats are stored in the workbook: find them at the bottom of the Custom list.
Reuse one anywhere with Format Painter.

steps.say: On a Mac, the dialog is the same: Command 1, Number, Custom. To type the rupee sign, use the Indian English keyboard layout, or press Control, Command and Space to open Emoji and Symbols.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Format Cells: ⌘ + 1 > Number > Custom
Typing ₹: Indian English keyboard, or ⌃ + ⌘ + Space (Emoji & Symbols)

steps.say: To recap. Conditions in square brackets give lakh and crore commas. A trailing comma divides by a thousand, and crores need a formula. And labels belong in the format, never typed into the cell.

acts.t:
Recap
• [>=10000000] and [>=100000] sections give Indian grouping
• A trailing comma divides by 1,000; crores need =value/10000000
• Put labels in the format, not in the cell, so numbers still add up

steps.say: Your challenge. In H2 to H11, show the marketing spend in lakh, like 8.45 L. Divide by one lakh with a formula, then add a custom format with an L label. The answer is on S02-03 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
H2:H11: marketing spend in lakh, e.g. ₹8.45 L
Hint: =C2/100000, then a custom format like "₹"0.00" L"

Answer: sheet S02-03 Done

lessons.title: Cell styles, themes and table styles
learn: Change the whole workbook's look with a theme
lessons.mac:
Home > Cell Styles  •  Home > Format as Table  •  Page Layout > Themes
Table options: the Table Design tab
Excel for the web: table styles yes, themes no

steps.say: Here's an expense claims list styled in a few clicks: a Title style on top, a banded table with a total row, and a colour theme that sets the look of the whole workbook. Change the theme, and everything built on it changes together.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S02-04 Done

steps.say: You'll apply cell styles, turn a range into a styled table with a total row, and change the workbook theme. Themes aren't available in Excel for the web, so this lesson is recorded in the desktop app.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• One-click headings with Cell Styles
• Table styles and a total row
• Change the whole workbook's look with a theme

Practice sheet: S02-04
Recorded in Excel desktop (themes are not in Excel for the web)

steps.say: Cell styles are named looks, like Title, Heading 1 and Total. Table styles format a whole table at once. Both take their colours and fonts from the theme, while colours you pick by hand don't.

acts.t:
Three layers of consistent formatting
Cell Styles: Title, Heading 1-4, Total, Good, Bad, Neutral, Input, Note
Table styles: header, banded rows and total row in one click
Themes: one set of colours and fonts for the workbook
Styles follow the theme. Hand-picked colours don't.

steps.say: Select the title in A1. On the Home tab, open Cell Styles and choose Title. One click sets the size, the weight and a theme colour.
Now select the data, A3 to F15. Click Format as Table and pick Table Style Medium 2. Check that My table has headers is ticked, and click OK. Banded rows and filter buttons appear.
On the Table Design tab, tick Total Row. Excel adds a total under the Amount column, sixty-three thousand two hundred and thirty-five rupees. It uses SUBTOTAL, so it also works when you filter.
Now the theme. On the Page Layout tab, open Themes and choose Retrospect. The title, the table and the colours all change together, because they use theme colours.
Except one thing. The line in A2 kept its dark blue. Someone coloured it by hand with a fixed colour, so the theme can't touch it. That's how reports end up with clashing colours.
Fix it with a style. With A2 selected, choose Cell Styles, Heading 4. Now it follows the theme like everything else.
Switch back to see it work both ways. Choose Page Layout, Themes, Office. The title, the table and A2 all move back together.
If your company has brand colours, set them once under Page Layout, Colors, Customize Colors, and save the theme. Every style and table then uses your brand.

acts.t:
Pro tip
Page Layout > Colors > Customize Colors: enter your brand colours once.
Save the theme, and every style, table and chart picks them up.

steps.say: On a Mac, Cell Styles and Format as Table are on the Home tab, and Themes are on the Page Layout tab, just like here. The table tab is called Table Design. Excel for the web has table styles, but not themes.

acts.t:
Mac corner
Home > Cell Styles  •  Home > Format as Table  •  Page Layout > Themes
Table options: the Table Design tab
Excel for the web: table styles yes, themes no

steps.say: To recap. Cell styles give consistent headings in one click. Table styles add banding and a total row. And themes restyle everything that uses them, so avoid hand-picked colours.

acts.t:
Recap
• Cell Styles for headings and totals
• Format as Table + Total Row
• Themes restyle everything built on them; manual colours don't follow

steps.say: Your challenge. Use the filter button on Approved to show only Yes. Read the total row, and type that figure in I3. Then clear the filter. The answer is on S02-04 Done.

acts.t:
Challenge
Filter Approved = Yes, read the Total Row, and type the amount in I3.
Then clear the filter.

Answer: sheet S02-04 Done

lessons.title: Freeze panes, split and views
learn: Page Layout and Page Break views
lessons.mac:
View tab: Freeze Panes, Freeze Top Row, Freeze First Column, Split
Menu bar: View > Normal / Page Layout / Page Break Preview

steps.say: This GST sales register has 150 invoices and eleven columns. In the finished version, the heading row and the first three columns stay on screen however far you scroll. A small setting that makes long sheets readable.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S02-05 Done

steps.say: You'll freeze rows and columns, split the window, and switch between Normal, Page Layout and Page Break Preview. Split and the page views aren't in Excel for the web, so this lesson is recorded in the desktop app.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Keep headers visible while scrolling
• Split one sheet into two panes
• Page Layout and Page Break Preview

Practice sheet: S02-05
Recorded in Excel desktop (Split and page views are not in Excel for the web)

steps.say: Freeze Panes keeps everything above and to the left of the selected cell in place. Split gives you two or four panes of the same sheet that scroll separately.

acts.t:
View tab
Freeze Panes: rows above and columns left of the selected cell stay put
Freeze Top Row  •  Freeze First Column
Split: two or four panes that scroll separately
Normal  •  Page Layout  •  Page Break Preview

steps.say: On the practice sheet, jump to the bottom with Command and the down arrow. The headings have gone, so you can't tell column G from column K without scrolling back up.

First, Split. Go back to the top, select A75, and on the View tab click Split. You get two panes of the same sheet, each with its own scroll bar, so you can compare the first invoices with the last ones.
Click Split again to remove it.
The View tab also has page views. Page Layout shows the sheet as printed pages, with margins, and headers and footers you can click into.
Page Break Preview shows where each page ends, with blue lines you can drag to fit more on a page.
Click Normal to come back.
Now freezing. A common slip is to select a cell in the middle, like A10, and click Freeze Panes. Excel freezes everything above row 10: nine rows that eat half the screen.
Go back to the top and choose Freeze Panes, Unfreeze Panes.
The rule: select the cell just below the rows, and just right of the columns, that you want to keep. We want row 1 and column A, so select B2, and choose Freeze Panes.
Jump to the bottom, then to the far right. The headings stay at the top, and the invoice numbers stay on the left.
Freeze Panes is saved with the file, so everyone who opens it sees the same frozen headings. Go back home to A1 before you save, so the sheet opens at the top.
On a Mac, Freeze Panes, Freeze Top Row, Freeze First Column and Split are all on the View tab. The page views are also in the View menu in the menu bar.

acts.t:
Mac corner
View tab: Freeze Panes, Freeze Top Row, Freeze First Column, Split
Menu bar: View > Normal / Page Layout / Page Break Preview

steps.say: To recap. Select the cell below and to the right of what you want to keep, then Freeze Panes. Split compares two parts of one sheet. And Page Break Preview shows where the pages end.

acts.t:
Recap
• Freeze = select the cell below and right of what stays, then View > Freeze Panes
• Split compares two parts of a sheet
• Page Layout and Page Break Preview before you print

steps.say: Your challenge. Change the freeze so that row 1 and the first three columns, invoice number, date and customer, stay visible. S02-05 Done is frozen that way.

acts.t:
Challenge
Keep row 1 and columns A:C visible while scrolling.
Hint: unfreeze, select D2, freeze.

Answer: sheet S02-05 Done

lessons.title: Pictures, icons and shapes
learn: Insert a logo and place a picture in a cell
Shapes and text boxes for notes
lessons.mac:
(Excel for Mac app)
Insert > Pictures > Picture from File, or Place in Cell
Insert > Icons: free icon library     Insert > Text Box: plain note box
Shapes: choose one, then drag on the sheet to draw it

steps.say: This product catalogue has the company logo at the top, a photo inside each product's row, and a note in a rounded box. Pictures and shapes make a sheet easier to read when it goes to distributors or a sales team.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S02-06 Done

steps.say: You'll insert a logo over the cells, place product photos inside cells, and add a shape with text for a note. The practice sheet is S02-06, and the four picture files are in the same folder as the workbook.

acts.t:
In this lesson
• Insert a logo over the cells
• Place a picture inside a cell
• Shapes with text for notes

Practice sheet: S02-06
Picture files: S02_logo.png, S02_rice.png, S02_tea.png, S02_masala.png

steps.say: A picture placed over cells floats on top of the grid, which suits a logo. A picture placed in a cell becomes the cell's content, so it moves, sorts and filters with its row.

acts.t:
Insert > Pictures
Place over Cells: floats on top. Good for logos and banners
Place in Cell: lives inside the cell, moves with its row
Insert > Shapes: boxes and arrows for notes. Type to add text

steps.say: Select A1. On the Insert tab, click Pictures, choose Place over Cells, then This Device. Pick the file S02 logo, and click Open.
The logo floats over the cells. To resize it, drag a corner handle, not a side, so it keeps its shape.
For product photos, many people do the same thing. Select A6 and insert the rice photo over the cells.
It floats over A6, but it isn't part of the row. Sort or filter the table and the photo stays where it is while the data moves, so photos end up next to the wrong products. Undo with Command Z.
Instead, select A6 and choose Pictures, Place in Cell, This Device, and pick the rice photo. It sits inside the cell, sized to fit, and travels with its row.
Do the same for the tea in A7 and the garam masala in A8.
Now a note for the sales team. Select G5, then on the Insert tab open Shapes and choose Rectangle, Rounded Corners. With the shape selected, start typing: Prices valid till 31-03-2027.
Press Escape when you've finished typing. Drag the shape by its border to place it beside the table, and use the Shape tab for its fill and outline colours.
Add alt text to every picture: right-click it, choose Edit Alt Text, and describe it in a few words. Screen readers read it out, and it helps anyone who receives the file.

acts.t:
Pro tip
Control-click a picture > Edit Alt Text
Describe it in a few words, e.g. 'Sahyadri Basmati Rice, 5 kg bag'

steps.say: In the Mac app, Insert, Pictures also gives Picture from File and Place in Cell. Insert, Icons opens a free icon library, and Insert, Text Box adds a plain box for longer notes. Shapes there are drawn by dragging on the sheet.

acts.t:
Mac corner (Excel for Mac app)
Insert > Pictures > Picture from File, or Place in Cell
Insert > Icons: free icon library     Insert > Text Box: plain note box
Shapes: choose one, then drag on the sheet to draw it

steps.say: To recap. Logos go over the cells. Product photos go in the cell, so they move with their rows. And shapes with text make neat notes.

acts.t:
Recap
• Logos: Place over Cells
• Photos in a table: Place in Cell
• Shapes and text boxes for notes; add alt text

steps.say: Your challenge. Give the note a light yellow fill and a dark yellow outline, like on S02-06 Done. Then add alt text to the logo.

acts.t:
Challenge
Note shape: light yellow fill, dark yellow outline
Add alt text to the logo

Compare with sheet S02-06 Done

lessons.title: Challenge 2: format a monthly expense report
learn: Turn a plain sheet into a report you can send

steps.say: Here's a plain monthly expense report from the Mumbai sales office. Your job is to turn it into a report you'd be happy to email to your manager.
The seven tasks are listed from column J: the title, the heading row, dates, rupee formats, a percentage, borders, and frozen headings.
Pause the video now and try all seven tasks on sheet S02-07. When you're done, press play to watch the solution.

acts.t:
Your turn
Pause now and complete the seven tasks on sheet S02-07.
Press play when you're done to see the solution.

Answers: sheet S02-07 Answers

steps.say: Here's the solution. Task one. Select A1, press Command B, and click Increase Font Size twice, to 14. Then select A1 to F1, press Command 1, and on the Alignment tab choose Center Across Selection.
Task two. Select A4 to F4, press Command B, pick Dark Blue from Fill Color and White from Font Color, then click Wrap Text. Centre B4 to F4 as well.
Task three. Select the dates, A5 to A16, open Format Cells, choose Custom, and type d d, dash, m m, dash, y y y y.
Task four. In the Name Box, type D5 colon F17, a comma, then F19 colon F20, to select both ranges at once. Open Format Cells, choose Custom, and enter the lakh and crore format from lesson three.
Task five. Select F21, open Format Cells, and choose Percentage with one decimal place. Budget used reads 78.7 percent.
Task six. Select A4 to F17 and choose Borders, All Borders. Then select the total row, A17 to F17, press Command B, and choose Top and Double Bottom Border.
Task seven. Select A5, and choose View, Freeze Panes, Freeze Panes. Rows 1 to 4 now stay on screen as you scroll.
Compare your sheet with S02-07 Answers. The total spend is three lakh fourteen thousand nine hundred and twenty-four rupees, within the four lakh budget.

acts.h: Go to the sheet S02-07 Answers

steps.say: Well done. You used fonts, fills, borders, Center Across Selection, custom number formats and Freeze Panes on one real report. Next, we start writing formulas.

acts.t:
Section 2 skills used
• Center Across Selection, fills and borders
• Custom date and lakh-crore formats
• Percentages and Freeze Panes

Next: Section 3, formula foundations
